usage: for small flat or round objects — stamps, coins, badges, rings and medals; a neutral, slightly formal choice (一枚邮票).
example: 信封上贴着一枚邮票。
exampleEn: There is a stamp stuck on the envelope.

usage: for lamps and lights (一盏灯); classically also for cups of tea or wine (一盏茶).
example: 书房里亮着一盏台灯。
exampleEn: A desk lamp is on in the study.

usage: for thin wispy things: strands of hair, threads of smoke, rays of light or fragrance (一缕阳光, 一缕炊烟).
example: 一缕阳光从窗户照进来。
exampleEn: A ray of sunlight came in through the window.

usage: for strands of rope or hair, currents of air or water, whiffs of smell and surges of feeling (一股寒流, 一股香味); in finance, shares (一股股票).
example: 厨房里飘来一股香味。
exampleEn: A delicious smell drifts out of the kitchen.

usage: for a streak or lingering trace of light, colour or a smile spread over a surface (一抹晚霞, 一抹微笑).
example: 天边还剩一抹晚霞。
exampleEn: Only a streak of evening glow remains on the horizon.

usage: for plants growing thickly together — a clump, cluster or thicket (一丛灌木, 一丛野草).
example: 河边长着一丛野草。
exampleEn: A clump of wild grass grows by the river.

usage: for buildings — close in meaning to 栋, common in written and news Chinese (一幢大楼).
example: 河对岸又盖起了一幢大楼。
exampleEn: Another high-rise has gone up across the river.

usage: for things tied together in a bundle (一捆柴, 一捆书).
example: 他抱着一捆书走进教室。
exampleEn: He carried a bundle of books into the classroom.

usage: for batches or groups of people moving or acting together (一拨人); reduplicated, 一拨一拨 = in wave after wave.
example: 游客一拨接一拨地走进博物馆。
exampleEn: Visitors streamed into the museum group after group.

usage: for animals born or kept together in one nest or litter (一窝小猪, 一窝小鸟); 一窝蜂 = swarming like bees.
example: 母鸡孵出了一窝小鸡。
exampleEn: The hen hatched a brood of chicks.

usage: for litters of baby animals born at one birth, and for births in a family (一胎, 第二胎).
example: 她家的猫一胎生了四只小猫。
exampleEn: Her cat gave birth to four kittens in one litter.

usage: for a cut-off section or segment of something long: wood, rope, a road or text (一截木头, 一截路).
example: 地上有一截断掉的绳子。
exampleEn: There is a length of broken rope on the ground.

usage: for matters, cases and deals seen as one whole item (一桩心事, 一桩案子, 一桩喜事).
example: 这桩婚事两家都很满意。
exampleEn: Both families are very pleased with this marriage.

usage: a formal classifier for deals, transactions, cases and matters (一宗买卖, 一宗案件).
example: 这宗案件还在调查中。
exampleEn: This case is still under investigation.

usage: for acts and scenes of a play (第一幕, 三幕剧); figuratively, for episodes of real events (一幕悲剧, 一幕幕往事).
example: 这场戏一共有三幕。
exampleEn: This play has three acts in total.

usage: for classes or lessons — a more formal counterpart of 节 (一堂课); also for sets of furniture (一堂家具).
example: 今天下午有一堂英语课。
exampleEn: There is an English class this afternoon.

usage: formal — for a talk or piece of advice (一席话 = a speech); in fixed phrases for a place or position (一席之地); for banquet tables (一席酒宴).
example: 听君一席话，胜读十年书。
exampleEn: Hearing your words is worth more than ten years of reading.

usage: for schools and factions of thought (两派意见); with 一, for a full scene or manner (一派春光, 一派胡言).
example: 公园里花都开了，真是一派春光。
exampleEn: The park is full of blooming flowers — a real scene of spring.

usage: for items of written or reported content: pieces of news, notices, fables and jokes (一则新闻, 一则寓言).
example: 这则新闻在网上传得很快。
exampleEn: This piece of news spread quickly online.

usage: for a dose or prescription of medicine, especially one whole batch of herbal medicine (一剂药, 一剂汤药).
example: 大夫给他开了三剂中药。
exampleEn: The doctor prescribed him three doses of herbal medicine.

usage: for small round pills or boluses, especially of Chinese medicine (一丸药).
example: 这种药一天吃三次，一次三丸。
exampleEn: Take this medicine three times a day, three pills each time.

usage: for objects with a long shaft or pole — guns, steelyard balances and flags (一杆枪, 一杆秤).
example: 卖菜的老伯用一杆秤称苹果。
exampleEn: The vegetable vendor weighs apples with a steelyard balance.

usage: dàn — a shoulder-pole load, a traditional unit of about 50 kilograms (100 jin); still heard for grain and water (一担米).
example: 他挑着一担水走进院子。
exampleEn: He carried a shoulder-pole load of water into the courtyard.

usage: for a puddle or spread-out mess of liquid or soft matter on a surface (一摊水, 一摊烂泥).
example: 厨房地上有一摊油。
exampleEn: There is a puddle of oil on the kitchen floor.

usage: ten days — a month divides into 上旬/中旬/下旬 (first/middle/last ten days); with age, 八旬 = eighty years old.
example: 他爷爷已年过八旬，身体依然很好。
exampleEn: His grandfather is past eighty and still in good health.

usage: tòng — for one complete run of an action such as a phone call, a scolding or a rant (一通电话); often right after a verb.
example: 他给家里打了一通电话。
exampleEn: He made a phone call home.

usage: mu — the standard Chinese land unit, about 666.7 square metres (1/15 of a hectare); still used for farmland (三亩地).
example: 他家承包了二十亩地种水稻。
exampleEn: His family contracted twenty mu of land to grow rice.

usage: hectare — 10,000 square metres (15 mu); used for farmland, parks and forest area.
example: 这个森林公园占地五百公顷。
exampleEn: This forest park covers 500 hectares.

usage: cubic metre — the standard unit of volume for water, air, concrete and wood (三立方米).
example: 这个水箱能装两立方米水。
exampleEn: This tank can hold two cubic metres of water.

usage: pound — a unit of weight equal to about 454 grams, used for coffee, meat, butter and body weight (一磅).
example: 我买了一磅咖啡豆。
exampleEn: I bought a pound of coffee beans.

usage: horsepower — a unit of engine power used for cars and machines (一百马力).
example: 这辆车的发动机有两百马力。
exampleEn: This car’s engine has 200 horsepower.

usage: a stack of flat things piled neatly one on another — books, plates or bowls (一摞书); also a verb, to pile up.
example: 书桌上放着一摞书。
exampleEn: A stack of books sits on the desk.

usage: a thick pile of flat things, especially paper money or documents (一沓钞票, 一沓纸).
example: 他从包里拿出一沓钞票。
exampleEn: He took a wad of banknotes out of his bag.

usage: a pinch of something fine or powdery, taken between the fingers — salt, sugar or tea leaves (一撮盐).
example: 煮汤时放一撮盐就够了。
exampleEn: A pinch of salt is enough when cooking the soup.

usage: frame — a single still image in a video, animation or film (一帧画面); 逐帧 = frame by frame.
example: 这段视频的每一帧都很清晰。
exampleEn: Every frame of this video is very clear.

usage: for a pool or puddle of clear liquid, especially water (一汪水, 一汪清泉).
example: 雨后院子里积了一汪水。
exampleEn: After the rain, a puddle of water gathered in the yard.

usage: (literary) for a body of clear water — a spring, lake or pool (一泓清泉, 一泓秋水).
example: 山间流淌着一泓清泉。
exampleEn: A clear spring flows in the mountains.

usage: for a lock or wisp of hair hanging loosely (一绺头发).
example: 她耳边垂着一绺头发。
exampleEn: A lock of hair hangs by her ear.

usage: (colloquial) for a lump or clump of soft or sticky stuff — mud, dough or ice (一坨泥).
example: 鞋底沾了一坨泥。
exampleEn: A lump of mud is stuck to the sole of the shoe.

usage: for crops grown and harvested in one cycle (一茬韭菜); figuratively, for a batch or generation of people (这茬年轻人).
example: 韭菜割完还能再长一茬。
exampleEn: After leeks are cut, another crop can still grow.

usage: for things growing or gathered closely in a cluster — flowers, grass or flames (一簇鲜花, 一簇火苗).
example: 花瓶里插着一簇鲜花。
exampleEn: A cluster of flowers stands in the vase.
